# Hierarchical-Complexity @ Stage 7 — Sentential & Faith

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 74 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Hierarchical-complexity at Order 5 is **questioning hierarchy**: the first moment where
the agent evaluates its inherited structural rules against emerging evidence and
reasoning. "But is this structural arrangement really correct?" The child who asks "Why
do we build it THIS way?" is performing the cognitive operation that will eventually
produce complexity theory and systems engineering.

The key advance from Stage 6 is **structure-evaluation**. The agent can now step back
from its inherited structural rules and ask whether they meet some standard of
correctness independent of tradition itself. "My teacher said to build it this way, but
it doesn't seem stable" is a Stage 7 hierarchical insight.

But hierarchical reasoning at Stage 7 is still **concrete and particular**. The agent
can evaluate specific structural arrangements against specific criteria, but cannot yet
construct abstract theories of hierarchical complexity.

Faith-based structural behavior emerges at Stage 7. The agent chooses structural
patterns based on transcendent commitment: "We build this way because it is right, not
because our ancestors told us." This is a genuine advance over Stage 6 — the structure
is now chosen, not just inherited.

The transition from Stage 7 to Stage 8 occurs when the agent can construct abstract
theories of hierarchical complexity.

In human development, Stage 7 corresponds to the pre-teen who begins to question
structural methods: "Why do we build it THIS way?"

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural structural systems are now subject to internal critique.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate structural rules against evidence and
  reasoning.

- **LL:** Institutions emerge that encode structure-evaluation: schools of
  engineering, structural societies, design-based education.

- **LR:** The library, the structural salon, the engineering debate.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Self-righteous structural imposition — forcing one's own
  structure evaluation on others.

- **Dark allergy:** Refusal to question inherited structural rules.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to one's own structure evaluation as the only valid
  perspective.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all structure evaluation as subjective.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Structure evaluation:** The agent evaluates structural rules against evidence
  and reasoning.

- **Faith-based hierarchy:** The agent chooses structural patterns based on
  transcendent commitment.

- **Concrete method evaluation:** The agent can evaluate specific structural
  arrangements but cannot construct general theories.

- **Hierarchical voice:** The agent challenges inherited structural rules when it
  perceives inconsistency.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Commons, R.A. et al. (1998). *Hierarchical Complexity of Tasks* — Order 5 as the
  first sentential operations
- Piaget, J. (1952). *The Origins of Intelligence in Children* — the transition to
  formal operations
- Kegan, R. (1982). *The Evolving Self* — the third-order hierarchical transition
